body.title: Per-family model definitions served by the daemon

summary.prose: insrc will hold one authoritative description of each model family it supports and of the models in it, kept by the background service and shared with every screen that shows or changes model settings. Updating to a new model or version becomes a data change rather than a code change, every client shows exactly what the service will run, and a model insrc does not yet know is checked and approved by the user before it is used.

body.problem: The facts that describe each model family insrc can run on (the Claude CLI, the Codex CLI and local Ollama) are scattered rather than held in one place. Runner identity and family-specific behaviour are repeated as literal strings and per-family branches across the daemon, the terminal UI and both IDE plugins. Model ids are written in several places: the tier defaults (src/config/analyze.ts:135-137), the config-catalog defaults (src/config/config-catalog.ts:116-118), the summariser fallback (src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:271), the curated catalog asset (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json:5 and src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json:11) and the installer's Codex tier block (scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh:295-297, copied at vscode-plugin/assets/insrc-daemon-install.sh:295-297). Reasoning-effort levels are one fixed list shared by every model (src/config/analyze.ts:115), not a per-model fact. Input size is described per family, not per model: every Codex model shares one fixed character budget (CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS, src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:181, chosen by CLI kind at src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:204); no Claude model has one, so Claude's own size refusal decides (classifyInputTooLarge reads its "Prompt is too long" at src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:743); and every Ollama model used for analysis gets the one global context window (models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx, default 32768, src/config/analyze.ts:216), passed at src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:267, src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:303, src/analyze/context/driver.ts:531 and src/analyze/context/driver.ts:833. ModelParams.maxInputTokens (src/shared/types.ts:417) is declared but read nowhere. The same fact is therefore stated many times and can drift: a client can offer an effort level or a model the daemon will not honour, or the daemon can run a model with a capability it lacks, and nothing notices. Model releases arrive often (new versions, new effort levels that only some models support), and today each one needs edits in several of the places above before anyone can use it. The clients already take their model lists from the daemon's providers.listModels request (registered at src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts:1430, served from the catalog at src/daemon/list-models.ts:127, and called at vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts:436 and jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/settings/ModelTiersSection.kt:195), but both IDE plugins keep their own runner list (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:30 and vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:78-80; jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/settings/ModelTiersModel.kt:34). The effort levels are themselves stated twice in the daemon: as TIER_EFFORTS (src/config/analyze.ts:115) and again as literal enum values in the config catalog's effort rows (src/config/config-catalog.ts:120). The VS Code plugin imports that config catalog into its own bundle (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:25) and takes its effort choices from those rows (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:199), so a new effort level also needs a VS Code release. When a user picks a model that insrc does not know, there is no record of what that model can actually do: a tier stores only a runner (src/config/analyze.ts:107), a model (src/config/analyze.ts:108) and an optional effort (src/config/analyze.ts:111), and a catalog entry only an id (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:43) and a display name (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:44), so its effort levels and limits are guessed rather than known. The cost falls on every model update and on every user who switches models: slow, error-prone changes, and settings screens that may not match what actually runs.

nonGoals.text: User-defined model families or runner implementations.
nonGoals.rationale: Families and their transport stay built in [[c1]].

nonGoals.text: Migrating only the daemon and TUI.
Migrating every consumer in one coordinated release.

nonGoals.rationale: A model update must not need a code change [[c2]].

nonGoals.text: Making every model-level fact configurable (transport, structured-output handling).
nonGoals.rationale: Configuration is limited to model selection and capability overrides [[c1]].

nonGoals.text: A shared versioned definition package, or mirrored definitions in each client.
nonGoals.rationale: The daemon is the single authority over IPC [[c1]].

nonGoals.text: Silently treating an unknown model with conservative or inherited family defaults.
nonGoals.rationale: An explicit, user-approved capability profile is required [[c3]].

nonGoals.text: Per-repo overrides of a tier's runner, model or effort.
nonGoals.rationale: Tier settings are global; a repo only chooses which tier a role uses, and existing per-repo tier overrides are removed [[c13]].

assumptions.text: The existing curated model catalog keeps its file (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json), its loader (validateModelCatalog, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:162) and its boot hook (src/daemon/index.ts:381); its types and validator are extended rather than replaced: today validateShape (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:107) keeps only id and displayName per entry (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:141-144) and only the two CLI families (iterated at src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:124 into a map typed to those two at src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:120 and returned at src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:151), so the per-model facts and an Ollama family need new fields in CloudModelCatalogFile (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:48) and a stricter validateShape.

Each CLI's response to an unknown model or effort is observable: both reject an unknown model with exit 1; codex rejects an unknown effort value with exit 1 while claude warns and exits 0; but codex runs a known effort level that a given model does not list without any error, so a codex model's accepted levels must come from `codex debug models` rather than from a test run.
The Codex CLI lists its models and each model's supported reasoning levels locally via `codex debug models`; the Claude CLI has no equivalent listing command.

Tier defaults are resolved through resolveTier, reached both from the config path (resolveTiers) and directly from the TUI's effective-tier view; every caller of resolveTier and every direct read of DEFAULT_TIERS must take the shared description.

constraints.text: No direct cloud REST calls: model probing and listing go only through the locally installed claude and codex CLIs and local Ollama.
The daemon owns the definitions; the CLI, MCP server and IDE plugins reach them only over daemon IPC.
Probes that reach an LLM provider run serially, never concurrently.
Model-level facts live in a repo-shipped data file, not in code and not in the user's config.json.
An unknown model is usable only after the user approves its probed capability profile.
Tier settings (runner, model and effort) are global only; per-repo configuration may only choose which tier each role uses (and the core floor). Existing per-repo tier overrides are removed.

A missing or malformed definitions file is a fail-fast startup refusal, as the curated catalog is today. The daemon awaits validateModelCatalog (src/daemon/index.ts:381) before it starts listening (src/daemon/index.ts:456), so no request is served before the file is validated.

stories.title: Ship model definitions as data the daemon checks at startup
stories.userValue: A maintainer can add a new model, a new version or a new effort level by editing one shipped data file, with no code change, and a broken file is caught before the daemon serves anything.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the shipped definitions describe the Claude CLI, Codex CLI and Ollama families with their models, tier defaults, summariser model, per-model effort levels and input limits
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon starts
acceptanceCriteria.then: it loads those definitions once and holds them as the single source for every later request

acceptanceCriteria.given: a maintainer adds a model with its effort levels to the shipped definitions file and changes nothing else
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon is rebuilt and restarted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the new model and its effort levels are available without any code change

acceptanceCriteria.given: the definitions file is missing, malformed, names an unknown family, or gives a tier default that is not one of that family's models
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon starts
acceptanceCriteria.then: it refuses to start and logs which entry is wrong

functionalRequirements.statement: The model definitions for the three built-in families are read from a data file shipped with insrc, separate from the user's settings.
An invalid definitions file stops the daemon at startup with a message naming the faulty entry.

stories.title: Ask the daemon for family and model definitions
stories.userValue: Every client can show exactly the families, models, effort levels and limits the daemon will use, by asking the daemon instead of keeping its own list.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the daemon is running with valid definitions
acceptanceCriteria.when: a client asks for the model definitions
acceptanceCriteria.then: it receives every family with its models, each model's accepted effort levels and input limit, the tier defaults and the summariser model, in a shape that can also carry models the user approves later

acceptanceCriteria.given: a client asks for the models of a family
acceptanceCriteria.when: the existing model-list request is used
acceptanceCriteria.then: its answer is drawn from the same definitions and agrees with the full definitions answer

functionalRequirements.statement: Clients can request the complete family and model definitions from the daemon.
The existing per-provider model list agrees with the full definitions.

stories.title: The daemon runs every model by the shared definitions
stories.userValue: What the daemon actually runs (runner, default model per tier, summariser, effort passed to the CLI) always follows the definitions, so a model update takes effect everywhere at once and nothing runs with an effort level its model does not accept. A repo can still choose which tier each role uses, but no longer changes what a tier runs.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a tier has no model set in the user's settings
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon resolves that tier
acceptanceCriteria.then: it uses the tier default from the definitions, not a value written in code

acceptanceCriteria.given: a tier is set to a model and an effort level that model does not accept
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon resolves that tier
acceptanceCriteria.then: it does not pass the unsupported effort to the CLI and logs a warning naming the model and the effort

acceptanceCriteria.given: the daemon's routing, provider construction, attribution and workflow code
acceptanceCriteria.when: they name a runner, CLI kind or model
acceptanceCriteria.then: they take it from the definitions, and no runner or model name remains as a literal in that code outside the family implementations

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repo's settings choose which tier a role uses
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon resolves that role
acceptanceCriteria.then: the repo's choice of tier applies, while the tier's runner, model and effort come only from the global tier settings and definitions

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user's settings still carry a per-repo tier override (a runner, model or effort under a repo)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon starts or its settings are reconciled
acceptanceCriteria.then: the override is not used, a warning names the repo and tier, and the stale entry is removed from the settings

functionalRequirements.statement: Tier defaults, the summariser model and per-model effort and input limits used at run time come from the definitions.
An effort level a model does not accept is never sent to its CLI.
Runner and model names are no longer written as literals across the daemon.
A repo can choose only which tier each role uses; per-repo tier runner, model and effort overrides are no longer honoured and are removed from settings.

stories.title: Approve an unknown model after checking it against its CLI
stories.userValue: A user can choose a model insrc does not yet know, see what it actually supports when checked against its CLI, and decide whether to use it, instead of insrc guessing its capabilities.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user selects a model that is not in the definitions for its family
acceptanceCriteria.when: they ask to use it
acceptanceCriteria.then: insrc checks the model through its CLI, one check at a time: for the Codex CLI it takes the model's supported effort levels from the CLI's own model list and confirms the model runs; for the Claude CLI it confirms the model runs, reads the model's input limit from the CLI's JSON output, and confirms each claimed effort name is one the CLI recognises, because no Claude CLI output shows whether a given model supports a given level

acceptanceCriteria.given: the checks have finished
acceptanceCriteria.when: the results are shown to the user
acceptanceCriteria.then: each claimed effort level is shown with the CLI's evidence, for Codex as accepted or rejected and for Claude as rejected or as recognised with support the CLI cannot confirm, and the model is not used until the user approves which levels to allow

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user approves the checked profile
acceptanceCriteria.when: a tier is set to that model
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon accepts it with only the effort levels that passed their check and that the user approved

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user rejects the profile, or a check cannot reach the CLI
acceptanceCriteria.when: a tier is set to that model
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon refuses the model and says why

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user has approved a checked profile for a model that is not in the shipped definitions
acceptanceCriteria.when: a client asks the daemon for the model definitions
acceptanceCriteria.then: that model appears under its family, marked as user-approved, with only its approved effort levels

localConstraints.text: Checks reach the model only through the installed claude or codex CLI or local Ollama; no provider web API is called.
A codex run succeeding at an effort level is not proof the model supports that level; the CLI's own model list is the authority for codex.
No Claude CLI run shows whether a model supports an effort level; for a Claude model the user's approval, not a test run, admits each level, and the results say so.

functionalRequirements.statement: An unknown model is checked against its CLI per claimed effort level and the results are shown to the user.

requirements.statement: The system keeps one authoritative description of each built-in model family and of the models it offers, including tier defaults, the summariser model, the effort levels each model accepts and its input limit.
requirements.rationale: Removes the repeated, drifting statements of the same facts [[c1]].

requirements.statement: Model-level facts can be added or changed without a code change, from a data file shipped with insrc and separate from the user's personal settings.
The terminal UI and both IDE plugins obtain family and model descriptions from the background service and never keep their own copy.
requirements.rationale: Keeps what clients show consistent with what runs [[c1]].

requirements.statement: A user-selected model that is not in the shipped descriptions is checked against its CLI for each effort level it claims, the results are shown to the user, and the model is used only after the user approves it.
requirements.rationale: Unknown models need an explicit capability profile [[c3]].

requirements.statement: Every place that today names a runner, CLI kind or model by literal string reads it from the shared description instead, migrated in stages.
The model definitions for the three built-in families are read from a data file shipped with insrc, separate from the user's settings.
An invalid definitions file stops the daemon at startup with a message naming the faulty entry.
Clients can request the complete family and model definitions from the daemon.
The existing per-provider model list agrees with the full definitions.
Tier defaults, the summariser model and per-model effort and input limits used at run time come from the definitions.
An effort level a model does not accept is never sent to its CLI.
Runner and model names are no longer written as literals across the daemon.
An unknown model is checked against its CLI per claimed effort level and the results are shown to the user.
An unknown model is used only with the effort levels the user approved.
A repo can choose only which tier each role uses; per-repo tier runner, model and effort overrides are no longer honoured and are removed from settings.
